dedupe_keys.name: a standardized dataset of built up areas of china s cities with populations over 300 000 for the period 1990 2015

description: SUBAD-China contains standardized built-up area boundaries for 433 Chinese cities with populations over 300,000. The Science Data Bank page reports 2,598 shapefiles assembled in 35 listed files totalling 353.73 MB, along with validation points and confusion matrices. The series spans 1990 to 2015 at five-year intervals and uses the urban-agglomeration definition adopted by the United Nations World Urbanization Prospects. A modeller could use these boundaries to reconstruct historical settlement exposure or set urban growth scenarios for buildings and public services. The polygons describe built-up extent, not building footprints, population within each parcel or infrastructure network connections. The provider says Landsat and Sentinel inputs and manual post-processing were used to improve spatial and temporal consistency; the validation files should be consulted for accuracy limits. The files were not downloaded, so coordinate systems, geometry validity and all interval labels remain unchecked. The paper’s availability text calls the DOI an Open Science Framework record, but that DOI resolves to Science Data Bank, whose own page establishes identity and CC BY 4.0 rights. Related population and asset layers are needed to turn urban extent into network demand or exposure.
